analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 11.6.26
key_insights: Thursday's tech-led selloff was violent: Nasdaq -6.4%, SOX -12%, AI data-center levered names -12%, Momentum Long -11%. SPX had its worst day since April 2025 and NDX its worst since March 2020. Futures are bid this morning (Nasdaq +130bps).

Desk flows showed a steady drumbeat of supply across semis and data-center levered names with very limited defense. Volumes were heavy in SOXL, SOXX, SMH, QQQ and TQQQ, at or near records, and the desk calls it the highest put volume day ever.

Yesterday was the largest put day in CBOE history (more than 11mm puts traded). VVIX had its largest 1-day move since February 2018 and VXN had its largest 1-day change since Covid. The desk also received heavy incoming inquiries about fund and investor stress across the system.

GS Prime Brokerage: TMT funds fell more than 4% and are now roughly flat YTD, down from about +24% on average before the June/July AI sell-off. Global Fundamental LS managers fell 1.3% (a -2 SD move), mainly on market/beta exposure, and are +8.7% YTD. Multi-Strats fell 1.4% on high-beta names, Info Tech and Momentum (down 3.7 SD).
Systematic LS managers were up 0.2% yesterday and are +16% YTD, with US and EM Asia gains offsetting Europe and DM Asia losses.

Factors behind this morning's bounce: oversold conditions (SOX 14d RSI of 26, only two lower readings in a decade), a $25bn LRCX buyback (stock +11% pre-market), firmer European tech (ASML +7%, with the European desk moving to day 1sd to buy from 2sd to sell), and benign comments on data centers from the Texas governor-elect.

Earnings reactions pre-market: NET +20-21% on revenue re-acceleration and an above-Street guide, TEAM -16-17% as cloud growth underwhelmed against elevated expectations, ABNB +12% on a broad-based beat and raise, MCHP -1% on a below-Street F3Q guide, Unity +4% after hours on takeover talks.

Cloudflare revenue accelerated about 3.5pp to 39% y/y and was 6% above the Street. Q4 revenue is guided to +37.5% y/y, also 6% above. Management cited rising agentic traffic, with developers building agents on Workers up from 7mn to 10mn quarter on quarter, and customers burning through pool-of-funds commitments sooner.

Airbnb beat on gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA and raised FY26 revenue growth to the high-teens % from mid-teens. Negatives were Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin guided slightly down y/y, cancellation rates up to 19% from 16%, and take rates modestly below expectations because of the RNPL expansion.

Atlassian's cloud revenue grew +31% y/y against a guide of +28.5%, and FY cloud guidance was raised to 26% from 25.5%. The stock is still down because F2Q cloud revenue is guided to decelerate to about 27% y/y.

Microchip's quarter was in line, but F3Q27 revenue, gross margin and EPS were all guided below GS and the Street. Management said $53mn of unusual FY2Q revenue (licensing, price increases, contract revenue) makes the comparison harder.

Reuters reports Silver Lake and Saudi PIF held recent talks to buy Unity. The consortium discussed a valuation of about $25 billion before Unity's earnings lifted its market cap to roughly $21.5 billion. No deal is certain.
Elon Musk said on X that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 to make room for more Cybercab production.

GS Global Investment Research is framing risks to its US data center capacity forecasts after Democratic gubernatorial flips and campaigns featuring stricter data center regulation in Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia and Michigan.

Macro: NFP is due this morning with GS at +75k against +65k consensus (prior +29k), plus Fed speakers Musalem, Bowman and Daly. Overnight reports say Qatar's Emir spoke to Trump about de-escalating the Iran war.

Research updates: Lyft Buy with PT cut to $20 from $22, Live Nation Buy reiterated after a 3Q26 beat with focus shifting to Investor Day, Yelp Neutral with PT cut to $23 from $24, and Opendoor 3Q26 profitability delayed with weaker unit economics.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and cuts the 12-month PT from $22 to $20 after Q3'26. Adjusted EBITDA beat, North America rides growth accelerated for a second quarter, and shares trade at about 8x 2027 equity value to FCF-SBC.
3Q26 beat consensus on revenue, AOI, attendance and fee-bearing tickets. FY26 attendance is now expected to approach 180M fans. GS largely maintains its 2026+ AOI outlook.
GS keeps Neutral and trims the PT from $24 to $23. Other revenues grew +82% y/y but core advertising declined y/y on macro headwinds, and management plans to lean into investment.

earnings_insights: ABNB Q3'26 (reported, pre-market 11/6): gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA all beat GSe and Street estimates. FY26 revenue growth outlook raised to high-teens % y/y from mid-teens, adjusted EBITDA margin outlook at least 36% from at least 35.5%. Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin guided down slightly y/y. Cancellation rate 19% vs 16% a year ago, take rate modestly below GS/Street. New $12bn buyback authorization.
NET (reported): revenue 6% above the Street and +39% y/y, EPS 11% above the Street (FactSet). Q4 revenue guided to +37.5% y/y, 6% above Street, and Q4 EPS guided 13% above Street (FactSet).

TEAM F1Q (reported): cloud revenue +31% y/y vs guide +28.5%, subscription ARR +23% y/y, non-GAAP operating margin 32% vs guide 28.5%, FCF about $464mn. F2Q cloud revenue guided to about 27% y/y with non-GAAP operating margin about 26%. FY cloud revenue growth guide raised to 26% from 25.5%, operating margin to 25.5% from 25%.

MCHP F2Q (reported): revenue $1.62bn in line with GS $1.62bn and Street $1.61bn. Non-GAAP EPS $0.97 vs GS $0.96 and Street $0.94. Microcontroller revenue $775mn below GS $799mn and Street $803mn. F3Q27 guide (midpoint): revenue $1.61bn vs GS $1.65bn and Street $1.63bn, non-GAAP gross margin 64.5% vs GS 66.2% and Street 66.5%, non-GAAP operating margin 37.8% vs GS 39.4% and Street 39.0%, non-GAAP EPS $0.91 vs GS $0.98 and Street $0.95.

LYV 3Q26 (reported): revenue $10.11B vs consensus $9.60B, AOI $1.18B vs $1.15B, attendance 61.1M vs 56.7M, fee-bearing tickets 98.3M vs 91.5M. FY26 ticketing AOI growth now high-single-digit % (vs mid-single-digit prior), sponsorship AOI growth double-digit %. Higher 4Q26 pre-marketing expense expected.
LYFT Q3'26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA ahead of GSe/Street (FactSet). Management expects North America rides growth to accelerate again in Q4. Lyft Go membership launched with DASH.
YELP Q3'26 (reported): Other revenues +82% y/y, core advertising declined y/y across Services and RR&O. Management reiterates a $250m annualized Other revenue run rate exiting 2028.

OPEN 3Q26 (reported): contribution margin 3.3% vs GSe 5.1% and consensus 3.7%. Adjusted EBITDA loss -$31mn vs -$4mn in 2Q26. Homes sold 2,728, purchased 4,865. Listed inventory aged over 120 days rose to 18% from 9%. 4Q26 guide: revenue growth of at least 40% y/y with a $70-$85mn adjusted EBITDA loss. Management is behind schedule on its profitability targets.
